x_1x_2x_4+x_2x_3x_5+x_3x_4x_6+x_4x_5x_7+x_5x_6x_1+x_6x_7x_2+x_7x_1x_3\equiv 0\pmod 3.
\]

The seven triples are the seven lines of the Fano plane.

Let \(S\) be the support of the tuple, i.e. the set of indices where \(x_k\neq 0\). For \(k\in S\), write \(x_k=\pm 1\). A product term is nonzero modulo \(3\) exactly when its three indices all lie in \(S\).

For a support of size \(m\), suppose there are \(p\) entries equal to \(+1\) and \(m-p\) entries equal to \(-1\). The first condition is

\[
p-(m-p)=2p-m\equiv 0\pmod 3.
\]

We classify supports by their size and by how many Fano lines they contain.

---

### 1. Subset classification

The number of lines fully contained in a subset of size \(m\) is as follows.

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
m & \text{type of subset} & \text{number of contained lines}\\
\hline
0 & \varnothing & 0\\
1 & \text{any point} & 0\\
2 & \text{any pair} & 0\\
3 & \text{non-line} & 0\\
3 & \text{line} & 1\\
4 & \text{complement of a line} & 0\\
4 & \text{complement of a non-line} & 1\\
5 & \text{any 5-set} & 2\\
6 & \text{any 6-set} & 4\\
7 & \text{whole plane} & 7
\end{array}
\]

The counts of such subsets are

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
m & \text{number of subsets of each type}\\
\hline
0 & 1\\
1 & 7\\
2 & 21\\
3 & 28\text{ non-lines},\ 7\text{ lines}\\
4 & 7\text{ complements of lines},\ 28\text{ complements of non-lines}\\
5 & 21\\
6 & 7\\
7 & 1
\end{array}
\]

---

### 2. Supports containing no full line

If a support contains no full Fano line, then every product term is \(0\), so the second condition is automatic. We only need the sum condition.

The needed numbers of sign assignments with sum \(0\pmod 3\) are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
m & \text{valid sign choices per support} & \text{contribution}\\
\hline
0 & 1 & 1\\
1 & 0 & 0\\
2 & 2 & 21\cdot 2=42\\
3 & 2 & 28\cdot 2=56\\
4 & 6 & 7\cdot 6=42
\end{array}
\]

So the contribution from supports with no contained line is

\[
1+42+56+42=141.
\]

---

### 3. Supports containing exactly one line

If a support contains exactly one line, then the second expression is just the product on that line, which is \(\pm 1\), never \(0\pmod 3\). Thus these contribute

\[
0.
\]

This covers the \(7\) three-point lines and the \(28\) four-point complements of non-lines.

---

### 4. Supports of size \(5\)

Every \(5\)-set contains exactly two Fano lines, and those two lines intersect in one point.

For \(m=5\), the sum condition is

\[
2p-5\equiv 0\pmod 3 \implies p\equiv 1\pmod 3,
\]

so \(p=1\) or \(p=4\).

Let the two lines intersect at \(c\).

- If \(p=1\), there is one \(+1\). If it is at \(c\), both line-products are \(+1\), which fails. If it is at one of the other four points, one line-product is \(+1\) and the other is \(-1\), which works. This gives \(4\) assignments.
- If \(p=4\), there is one \(-1\). By the same reasoning, it works unless it is at \(c\). This gives another \(4\) assignments.

Thus each \(5\)-support contributes \(8\) valid sign assignments. There are \(\binom{7}{5}=21\) such supports, so the contribution is

\[
21\cdot 8=168.
\]

---

### 5. Supports of size \(6\)

A \(6\)-set is the complement of one point. The three lines through the omitted point partition the remaining six points into three pairs. The four lines not through the omitted point each choose one point from each pair.

For \(m=6\), the sum condition is

\[
2p-6\equiv 0\pmod 3 \implies p\equiv 0\pmod 3,
\]

so \(p=0,3,\) or \(6\).

- If \(p=0\) or \(p=6\), all four line-products are equal, so their sum is \(\pm4\not\equiv 0\pmod 3\). These fail.
- Thus \(p=3\).

Distribute the three \(+1\)'s among the three pairs.

If the distribution is \((1,1,1)\), then each pair has one \(+1\) and one \(-1\). In that case, all four line-products are equal, so the second condition fails.

Therefore the distribution must be a permutation of \((2,1,0)\): one pair is all \(+1\), one pair is all \(-1\), and one pair is mixed.

Choose:

- the all-\(+1\) pair: \(3\) ways,
- the all-\(-1\) pair: \(2\) ways,
- which point in the mixed pair is \(+1\): \(2\) ways.

So each \(6\)-support contributes

\[
3\cdot 2\cdot 2=12
\]

valid sign assignments. There are \(7\) six-point supports, giving

\[
7\cdot 12=84.
\]

---

### 6. Full support of size \(7\)

For \(m=7\), the sum condition is

\[
2p-7\equiv 0\pmod 3 \implies p\equiv 2\pmod 3,
\]

so \(p=2\) or \(p=5\).

If \(p=2\), a line-product is \(+1\) exactly when the line contains exactly one of the two \(+1\)'s. There are \(4\) such lines, so the line-product sum is

\[
4-(7-4)=1\not\equiv 0\pmod 3.
\]

If \(p=5\), this is the global sign flip of the \(p=2\) case, giving line-product sum \(-1\not\equiv 0\pmod 3\). Thus the full support contributes

\[
0.
\]

---

### 7. Total

Adding all contributions,

\[
141+168+84+0=393.
\]

\[
\boxed{393}
\]
